evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-tg has an unhealthy target. Diagnose the specific root cause and give me the corrected settings.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the target health (Target.Timeout), compares the health-check port (8080) against the target security group, finds the target SG allows 80 but not 8080 from the ALB SG, and classifies SG_BLOCK. Because the health-check port differs from the traffic port, it reports both fixes: point the health check back to traffic-port, or add the inbound rule (source = ALB SG, port 8080) if 8080 is an intentional dedicated health-check port.
assertions: The output classifies the cause as a security-group block on the health-check port
The output reports both corrected options: setting the health check back to the traffic port (80), and adding the inbound rule (source = ALB SG, port 8080) if 8080 is an intentional health-check port
The output labels the cause class as SG_BLOCK and presents the inbound rule as a change for the operator to apply, without modifying the security group itself

evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-lambda-tg behind the ALB nebula-demo-lambda-alb in us-east-1 has an unhealthy target. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report the corrected settings. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: The agent branches on target type first, recognizes Lambda targets have no target-side security group, and does not apply EC2 SG/NACL logic to them.
assertions: The output recognizes that Lambda targets do not have a target-side security group
The output does not apply EC2 security-group or NACL logic to the Lambda target
The output checks the function's resource policy for permission for elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com to invoke it, or checks the function's Errors/Throttles, or states why it could not

evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-web-tg behind the ALB nebula-demo-web-alb in us-east-1 has targets failing health checks with Target.Timeout, but the security groups and NACLs look correct. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report it. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: With the network path clean, the agent checks target resource utilization (CPU/credits/network/EBS burst, or ECS/EKS OOMKilled), compares across targets to see if exhaustion is isolated, and classifies RESOURCE_EXHAUSTION.
assertions: The output checks network or EBS burst metrics (NetworkIn/Out, BurstBalance, or EBSIOBalance%) before concluding
The output compares the targets in the group and identifies which are saturated and which are not
The output classifies the cause as RESOURCE_EXHAUSTION and leads the fix with the saturated dimension (for example CPU credits or instance size) rather than a longer health-check timeout
The output does not apply BurstBalance to a gp3 volume

evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-nacl-tg behind the ALB nebula-demo-nacl-alb in us-east-1 has targets failing health checks with Target.Timeout, and the security groups allow the health-check port. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report it. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the security groups are clean, then checks NACLs in both directions on both subnets, finds the target subnet NACL does not allow outbound ephemeral ports back to the load balancer subnets, and classifies NACL_BLOCK with the outbound entry to add.
assertions: The output classifies the cause as NACL_BLOCK
The output identifies the missing outbound ephemeral-port rule on the target subnet NACL as the cause, stating that NACLs are stateless
The output reports the NACL entry for the operator to apply without modifying the NACL itself

evals.prompt: Target nebula-demo-az-tg has a target showing unused with Target.NotInUse. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report it. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the reason code, compares the target's Availability Zone with the AZs enabled on the load balancer, finds the AZ is not enabled, and classifies ROUTABILITY without walking the security-group and NACL steps.
assertions: The output classifies the cause as ROUTABILITY
The output states the target's Availability Zone is not enabled on the load balancer and names the AZ or subnet to enable
The output does not report a security-group or NACL problem as the cause

evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-nlb-tg behind the NLB nebula-demo-nlb in us-east-1 has an unhealthy target. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report the corrected settings. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the NLB has no security group, so the target SG must allow the health-check port from the NLB's private IPs or the VPC CIDR instead of from a load-balancer SG, finds that rule missing, and classifies SG_BLOCK.
assertions: The output recognizes the NLB has no security group
The output classifies the cause as SG_BLOCK
The output reports the inbound rule with the NLB private IPs or the VPC CIDR as the source, not a load-balancer security group

evals.prompt: Target group nebula-demo-ecs-tg has IP targets from an ECS service using awsvpc networking and they are unhealthy with Target.Timeout. Diagnose the specific root cause now using read-only calls and report it. Do not ask clarifying questions or open a tracked investigation.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the targets are ECS awsvpc task ENIs, finds the task ENI's security group via the network interface, checks the health-check port against that SG, and reports the cause with the ECS service as the place to fix it.
assertions: The output identifies the target as an ECS awsvpc task with its own network interface
The output reads the security group from the task network interface, not from an EC2 instance
The output reports a specific cause class with the evidence observed
